[page[title]]

Turn operational evidence into an app-aware capability that can be queried, streamed and retained deliberately.

All platform domainsView the GitHub repositoryRead the documentation

What it owns

  • DB-backed ILogger provider and OData read/post endpoints.
  • Application-scoped log records with attached data.
  • SignalR streaming and scheduled retention cleanup.

Why the boundary matters

Support and engineering teams get a shared record of system behaviour without giving public callers permission to rewrite history.

How it fits

The domain is published and tested independently, then composed through cCoder.Core when an application needs the complete platform. That keeps ownership visible while preserving a straightforward application bootstrap.

Getting started

The source, current README, sample hosts and tests live in cCoder.Logging on GitHub. The repository README is the version-specific starting point; the outline below explains how the pieces fit together.

Reference the package

<PackageReference Include="cCoder.Logging" Version="YOUR_VERSION" />

During coordinated local development the repositories may substitute a sibling ProjectReference. Published applications should normally consume the agreed package version so the dependency boundary remains explicit.

Register it in the host

builder.Services.AddLoggingWeb(/* platform configuration */);
app.StartLoggingWeb();

Configure and run it

Configure Core persistence, application identity, the logging API route and retention policy. Use the HostedServices registration when scheduled retention cleanup runs in a worker process.

Consume the capability

Write through the supplied ILogger provider, query application-scoped LogEntry records through OData, and use SignalR streaming for live operational views. Attach structured LogDataItem values rather than hiding evidence in formatted strings.

Build and verify from source

git clone https://github.com/ccoder-co-uk/cCoder.Logging.git
cd cCoder.Logging
dotnet build
dotnet test

Use the repository-specific solution and test commands from its README when working on the domain itself; the standalone and acceptance-test hosts show the supported application boundary more accurately than an isolated snippet can.
